reconcile.note: Henry's own comment on Romans invokes Job to distinguish what of God may be apprehended from nature, enough for worship, from the full comprehension Job denies is possible.

discrepancy.note: Paine takes up Job's own question and answers it 'Yes,' arguing reason alone proves God's existence from nature, against the verse's implied denial.

quotes.text: First, Canst thou by searching find out God? Yes. Because, in the first place, I know I did not make myself, and yet I have existence…therefore it is, that I know, by positive conclusion resulting from this search, that there is a power superior to all those things, and that power is God.
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Parts I-II (1794-1795), on Job 11:7 and Romans 1:20.

sides.snippet: Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
sides.verseText: \"Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

sides.snippet: the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made
sides.verseText: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity; that they may be without excuse.
